findings.description: The spec vaguely states 'bounded retry window' without specifying poll-count semantics. The code implements a shared polling loop with early settlement when all symbols are numeric/permanently-errored or max_polls is reached. A1 and A2 diverge by inventing time-based Duration windows; A3 diverges with per-symbol retry counting. This is code-specific behavior the spec does not mandate.
findings.short_summary: Retry window is poll-count-based (max_polls), not time-based or per-symbol
findings.summary: The spec says 'bounded retry window' without specifying the bound mechanism. The code implements poll-count-based settling: a shared polling loop bounded by cfg.max_polls total polls, exiting early when all symbols are numeric/permanently-errored. A1 and A2 invent time-based Duration windows; A3 invents per-symbol retry counting. None match the code's shared-poll-window approach with latest-reading checks per symbol.
findings.failure_scenario: A1 or A2 timeout after time duration while code is still within max_polls window; A3 accumulates per-symbol transient count while code tracks only latest reading in a shared window. Given max_polls=4, symbol AMZN transient on polls 1,2,3,4: A3 marks degraded after retry_count≥max_retries (e.g., 2), but code waits for all 4 polls before checking latest reading.

findings.description: The code implements price_to_cents() with half-to-even rounding and defensive degradation for sub-cent/zero/negative/non-finite prices. The spec does not mention price conversion, rounding rules, or edge-case handling. None of the A outputs model this numeric conversion logic, which is critical to the marks-read interface.
findings.short_summary: Price-to-Cents conversion with half-to-even rounding and sub-cent/zero/non-finite degradation
findings.summary: The code implements price_to_cents() (lib.rs:362–385) converting USD to integer Cents via half-to-even rounding (pt_core::round_half_to_even applied at the cent boundary). Sub-cent prices (positive rounding to ≤0 Cents), zero, negative, and non-finite prices degrade as SubCent or Permanent. The spec does not mention price conversion, rounding rules, or these edge cases. None of the A outputs model this defensive numeric handling.
findings.failure_scenario: Price 1.005 USD: A outputs treat as valid 1.00 or 1.01 (impl-dependent float rounding); code applies half-to-even (→100¢), matching SHEET-MARK-005 from B reconstruction. Price 0.0001 USD: code degrades SubCent (test line 77–78); A outputs have no explicit model for sub-cent anomalies.

findings.description: The code distinguishes PriceReading::Permanent (terminal error) from Transient, degrading permanent errors immediately without retry and without prior mark carry-forward. The spec does not identify permanent vs. transient error types. None of the A outputs model this two-level error-handling strategy.
findings.short_summary: Permanent error immediate degradation without retry or prior carry-forward
findings.summary: The code has PriceReading::Permanent enum variant (terminal non-numeric error) that degrades immediately (lib.rs:881–882) without exhausting polling attempts and without attempting prior mark carry-forward. Transient errors retry and carry prior; permanent errors override prior and exit the retry window at once. The spec does not distinguish error types. None of the A outputs model permanent vs. transient bifurcation.
findings.failure_scenario: Symbol BADX returns Permanent on poll 1 of 8: code records degraded Permanent immediately (test line 240 confirms read_count < max_polls). A outputs lacking permanent-error case would either retry BADX through the full window or treat it as transient (wrong behavior).

findings.description: Marks are stamped with GOOGLEFINANCE quote_date (not wall-clock read time), and this quote-date is preserved when transient symbols carry forward prior marks. The spec does not mention quote-date handling or the distinction between quote epoch and read time. No A outputs model quote-date preservation.
findings.short_summary: Quote-date preservation via GOOGLEFINANCE quote epoch, not wall-clock read time
findings.summary: Marks carry a quote_date field stamped with the GOOGLEFINANCE-supplied quote epoch (lib.rs:858–861), not the wall-clock settle-pass timestamp. Transient carry-forward preserves the original quote-date from the prior cached mark (lib.rs:874–875). The spec does not mention quote-date handling or how to stamp marks over carry-forward cycles. None of the A outputs model quote-date preservation.
findings.failure_scenario: Cycle 1 marks AMZN at Date(19_180); Cycle 2 AMZN stays transient and carries prior mark: code preserves Date(19_180); A outputs have no explicit quote-date tracking and would lose or use current wall-clock time.
